text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The United Nations is preparing for two rounds of direct talks on Cyprus in New York and at a location in Switzerland at the beginning of July.
- Party leaders from the Greek and Turkish Cypriot sides meet, but the only thing they have agreed on is that they will meet again.
- Argentina's President Carlos Menem reviews the Argentine peacekeeping mission on the island.
- Dates have been set for bi-communal soccer matches.
- Parliament urges Cyprus to change its law to allow foreigners to apply for political asylum.
- Nicosia, Athens, and diplomatic sources in Cyprus have expressed pessimism on the outcome of the upcoming talks between President Glafcos Clerides and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash.
- Communist Akel says NATO should disband after the dissolution of the Warsaw Pact.

- Direct talks are looming, but without any expectations. The proximity talks do not appear to have shown any change in positions, while concern has been raised over the political instability in Turkey.
- The government issues new warnings to Cyprus Airways to clean up their act.
- Consultations among opposition parties to field a common candidate in presidential elections next year has turned into a labyrinth.
- Turkish businessmen attending a meeting with Greek Cypriots in Turkey at the weekend said they wanted two states in Cyprus with one economy.
